questions.q: In ETL, where does transformation happen relative to loading?
options: At the exact same moment as extraction, with no separate step
Before loading, in a dedicated transformation engine
Transformation never happens in ETL
After loading, inside the warehouse
questions.explain: ETL stands for Extract, Transform, Load — the transform step happens before the finished data is loaded into the warehouse.

questions.q: In ELT, what typically lands in the warehouse or lake first?
options: Raw, unchanged data
Only the final dashboard output
Nothing — ELT never stores raw data
Only pre-aggregated summary tables
questions.explain: ELT loads raw data as-is first, then transforms it in place using the warehouse's own compute — commonly via SQL or a tool like dbt.

questions.q: Why does ELT often produce lineage 'for free' compared to ETL?
options: Because ELT always uses CDC instead of full extracts
Because transformation logic is written as SQL/code that references other tables, so a tool can parse those references into a lineage graph automatically
Because ELT doesn't require an extraction step
Because ELT pipelines never have bugs
questions.explain: A dbt-style model's references to other models are themselves the lineage edges — a tool can parse the code and draw the dependency graph without separate documentation.

questions.q: Where does lineage typically live in an ETL pipeline?
options: Only in the source system's transaction log
In the orchestration tool's job definitions, which may or may not be documented
Automatically inside every SQL SELECT statement
It cannot exist in ETL pipelines at all
questions.explain: ETL lineage lives in job definitions (SSIS packages, Informatica mappings, etc.) — if undocumented, it must be reconstructed by reading the job's code.

questions.q: What made the ELT pattern practical at scale, according to the lesson?
options: The invention of CSV files
The retirement of all OLTP databases
Cheap cloud storage and elastic compute, which removed the need to decide what to discard before loading
A requirement that all data must be transformed exactly once
questions.explain: Cheap cloud storage and compute let teams load raw data first and decide later what transformations to apply, rather than transforming before anything lands.
